summary: Kurt Quecke was an Indology scholar who earned his Ph.D. in 1947 at the University of Marburg, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Johannes Nobel.
Kurt Schmidt was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Dr. iuris at the University of Rostock around 1898-1901. He founded the Buddhistische Arbeitsgemeinschaft in 1946.

Kurt Stegmann von Pritzwald was a linguist who studied at Giessen, Munich, and Jena (Ph.D. under Albert Debrunner). He taught at Jena, Kiel, Rostock, and the University of Marburg, becoming apl. Professor in 1945.

Kurt Tropper specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner and Michael Torsten Much, and has held posts at the University of Vienna and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Kurt Wulff was a linguistics and Sinology scholar. Educated at Copenhagen, Oxford, and Leipzig, he worked at the Thesaurus Linguae Latinae and the Royal Danish Library, later serving as Docent of East Asian Languages at Copenhagen from 1928.
Kurt von Kamptz was an Indologist who studied under Walther Schubring and received his Ph.D. from the University of Hamburg in 1929. He later worked as a librarian at Wehrkreisbücherei IV Dresden.

Kurtis R. Schaeffer is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Lewis & Clark, Evergreen State, Washington, and Harvard. He held faculty positions at the University of Alabama (2000-2004) and the University of Virginia (from 2005).
Kurunegoda Piyatissa worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, serving as head of the New York Buddhist Vihara (attested in 1998, with his post attested through 2009).

Kwangsoo Park is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned an MA at the University of Iowa and a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He is an attested professor at Wonkwang University (2020).

Kyo Kano is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Keio, Kyoto, and Vienna. He served as an assistant at Kyoto University (attested 1989) and became an associate professor (2000) and professor (2022) at Kobe Women's University.

Kyojun Shimizutani was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tendai Sect University and Taisho University. He served as a professor at both institutions and was head priest of Senso-ji from around 1952 to 1979.

Kyoko Amano is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Osaka University and the University of Freiburg. She held several academic posts at Osaka University and served at Kyoto University from 2013 to 2024.

Kyoko Fujii studied at the University of Tokyo and works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She held professorships at Yokohama City, Hamamatsu, Hokkaido, and ICPBS, and was director of the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (2020-2026).
Kyoko Tokuno is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who held positions at the University of Oregon and the University of Washington, where she was attested as a professor in 2017.
Kyokuga Saeki was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who trained under numerous traditional teachers, including Gen'yū. Around 1888 to 1891, he served as the 143rd abbot of Sennyu-ji.

Kyosho Hayashima was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. Over his career, he held teaching posts at Yokohama City University (1962), Toyo University (1962), and the University of Tokyo (attested 1980).
Kyosho Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He served as an associate professor at Musashino University from around 1976 to 2013.
Kyoshun Todo was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an associate professor (attested 1962) and later as a professor (attested 1988-1992) at Bukkyo University.

Kyozo Yamada was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied at the University of Tokyo. He founded Kamakura Haku-un-kai, served as the second head of Sanbo Zen from 1970, and worked at NOF Corporation.

Kyōtarō Nishikawa studied at Keio University and worked in history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He was Director-General of the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (1990-1996) and served at Kanagawa Prefectural Museum (1996-2008).
